raw.assessment: The incumbent offers a predictable, free conversational routine with a demonstrated paper channel. Seven frequent attendees value its repetition; the concrete limiting observation is five occasional attendees struggling to enter conversations already familiar to partners. Familiarity may help continuity while hindering entry, but causation is unestablished. Slips record useful practice on 49/72 occasions and correct preparation on 48/72; only 72 slips cover 97 attendances, speaking was not timed, and responses cannot be linked across weeks. Coordination sometimes exceeds 90 minutes. Current evidence does not establish the success targets.

openings.claim: Unequal familiarity with a conversation may reduce useful practice independently of time lost choosing partners.
openings.delta: Preserve the repeated session structure while testing a shared starting point within each pair.
openings.prediction: After pairing, a brief mutual reset using a fresh opening prompt will improve occasional attendees' useful-practice reports even if pair-formation duration remains similar.
openings.probe: Within existing practice time, alternate ordinary prompts and a fresh opening prompt with equal turns. Use anonymous observation to record formation time, each partner's speaking time, and partner changes; collect useful-practice reports with optional attendance-frequency categories. Compare conditions, especially occasional attendees, over six sessions and record volunteer minutes.
assumptions: A fresh shared prompt can reduce familiarity asymmetry without public proficiency labels.
Observed speaking duration supplements, rather than replaces, participants' judgments of usefulness.

openings.claim: Confusion between current and earlier preparation instructions may contribute to incorrect task identification; missing information remains an alternative explanation.
openings.delta: Test temporal clarity of the existing paper channel before adding coordination channels.
openings.prediction: Explicit session dates and one clearly marked next task will reduce earlier-task answers; persistent blank answers would suggest a different access or comprehension problem.
openings.probe: Use existing topic sheets with explicit current and next session dates, retain paper access and optional messaging, and make spare sheets available at each session. Track earlier-task errors separately from blanks and correct answers, including optional paper-only status, across six sessions; log printing and question-answering minutes against the 90-minute ceiling.
assumptions: Readers can interpret the dates and task wording.
Changing labels requires little additional volunteer effort.
No preparation completion or attendance history becomes a condition of participation.

raw.assessment: The supplied slips show preparation confusion and uneven reported practice, but do not establish their causes or represent every attendance. Pair formation and prior familiarity are plausible intervention points. Both openings are hypotheses requiring six-session outcome and workload checks.

openings.claim: Give every conversation a fresh information gap: each participant privately chooses an unseen prompt or personal example, then partners alternate explaining and asking. Offer optional printed sentence starters and deeper follow-up questions without proficiency labels. Begin with adjacent seats and permit partner changes.
openings.delta: A frequent attendee's familiarity becomes less decisive because neither partner knows the other's chosen content. Prompt support replaces public level assignment, while immediate seating reduces the initial matching decision.
openings.prediction: Compared with ordinary shared-sheet rounds, occasional attendees will report easier entry and more useful speaking, and observers will record shorter pairing delays and less unequal speaking time.
openings.probe: Counterbalance ordinary and fresh-gap rounds within sessions using existing sheets. Observe pairing delay and individual speaking duration anonymously; collect round-specific usefulness and entry-difficulty slips with optional attendance-frequency categories. Include accessible triad turn-taking when numbers are odd.
assumptions: Unknown partner content can create conversational interest at differing levels.
Participants can choose helpful support privately.
Printing and setup fit the weekly coordination budget.

openings.claim: Use a stable preparation invitation across weeks: choose one recent experience, object, or question to discuss. Put it on a reusable printed card, with optional weekly-topic examples. Reserve a session opening exchange for whatever participants brought or recalled; offer an immediate example to anyone arriving unprepared.
openings.delta: Preparation attaches to the participant's next attendance rather than a sequence of weekly assignments, potentially removing the earlier-task trap without penalizing absences.
openings.prediction: Task identification improves particularly among occasional attendees, preparation questions consume less volunteer time, and prepared material supports useful conversation.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, ask participants to describe their next preparation action and anonymously record whether their material supported useful speaking. Track all attendees, missing responses, and volunteer minutes by activity; assess the original three success thresholds together.
assumptions: A recurring invitation remains motivating and sufficiently clear.
Personal material can support conversation at participants' current levels.
Cards and reminders can be provided within existing resources.

openings.claim: A shared fresh start may reduce familiarity disadvantage independently of pairing delay.
openings.discriminator: Occasional attendees improve despite unchanged formation time.
openings.fit: Preserves repeated structure and voluntary participation.
openings.probe: Alternate ordinary and fresh prompts with equal turns; observe speaking, formation time and switches; collect usefulness by optional attendance frequency.
openings.uncertainty: Freshness may not resolve familiarity asymmetry.

openings.claim: Dates and one marked next task may resolve temporal confusion.
openings.discriminator: Earlier-task errors fall; blanks may indicate access or comprehension problems.
openings.fit: Existing paper, spare sheets and optional messages; no attendance prerequisite.
openings.probe: Date current/next sessions; distinguish correct, earlier and blank responses, optionally by paper-only use; log printing and questions.
openings.uncertainty: Date comprehension and low added workload are assumed.

openings.claim: Unseen personal content creates information gaps; private optional scaffolds support differing levels; adjacent seating reduces matching decisions.
openings.discriminator: Easier entry, shorter pairing delays and more balanced speech than ordinary rounds.
openings.fit: No public labels; allow switches and odd-number triads.
openings.probe: Counterbalance ordinary/fresh-gap rounds; alternate explaining/questions; observe individual speech and delay; collect round-specific usefulness and entry difficulty.
openings.uncertainty: Bundled mechanisms, support selection and setup cost remain uncertain.

openings.claim: A reusable invitation tied to next attendance may remove sequential-task confusion.
openings.discriminator: Occasional attendees identify preparation better; questions decrease while material supports conversation.
openings.fit: Printed card, optional topic examples and immediate examples for unprepared arrivals.
openings.probe: Invite an experience/object/question; include opening exchange; record next action, useful speaking, missing responses and coordination by activity.
openings.uncertainty: Recurring invitation may lose motivation or fail across levels.

post_distill.decision: Retain four hypotheses for six-session probes. Preserve free inclusive conversation, offline preparation, 75-minute room limit and no paid time. Check all thresholds together: 80% report ten useful minutes, 85% identify preparation, coordination below 90 minutes. Baseline is 72 unlinked slips across 97 attendances with no direct timing; causes and representativeness remain unknown.
